bib.title: Phi-3 Technical Report: A Highly Capable Language Model Locally on Your Phone
authors: Microsoft (author list alphabetical, led by Marah Abdin)

question: Can a 3.8B-parameter model trained on heavily filtered web data plus synthetic data match the benchmark quality of much larger models such as Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5 while running on a phone?
hypothesis: Data quality, not scale, drives small-model capability: filtering web data to the right 'educational level' and adding synthetic data moves a small model toward a 'data optimal regime'.
contributions: phi-3-mini (3.8B, 3.3T tokens) with performance rivalling Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5, runnable on a phone
phi-3-small (7B) and phi-3-medium (14B) trained on 4.8T tokens as parameter-scaling results
phi-3.5 series: phi-3.5-mini, phi-3.5-MoE (16x3.8B, 6.6B active) and phi-3.5-Vision (4.2B) for multilingual, long-context and multimodal use

method.summary: Decoder-only transformers trained in two sequential phases on filtered public web data and LLM-generated synthetic data, then SFT and DPO. Models are compared with other open and closed models on a fixed internal few-shot evaluation pipeline.
method.task: next-token pretraining of small language models, then SFT and DPO post-training

datasets.name: phi-3 pretraining mix phase 1
datasets.size: 3.3T tokens total for phi-3-mini; 4.8T for small and medium
datasets.source: heavily filtered publicly available web data (filtered by 'educational level'), plus synthetic LLM-generated data; not released
datasets.preprocessing: web data filtered to the right level of 'knowledge' and kept pages that may improve reasoning; e.g. daily sports results removed

datasets.name: phi-3 pretraining mix phase 2
datasets.source: even more heavily filtered web data (a subset of phase 1) merged with some synthetic data teaching logical reasoning and niche skills

datasets.name: SFT data
datasets.source: highly curated data in math, coding, reasoning, conversation, model identity, safety; starts with English-only examples

datasets.name: DPO data
datasets.source: chat format, reasoning and responsible-AI data; unwanted outputs used as rejected responses

datasets.name: Phi-3.5-Vision pretraining
datasets.source: interleaved image-text documents, FLD-5B image-text pairs, OCR synthetic data from PDFs, chart/table data, text-only data

datasets.name: Phi-3.5-Vision multimodal SFT
datasets.source: text SFT data, public multimodal instruct data, in-house multimodal instruct data

other.bos: BoS tokens removed, extra chat-template tokens added

models.name: phi-3-small
models.architecture: decoder, GEGLU activation, grouped-query attention (4 queries share 1 key), alternating dense and blocksparse attention layers

other.hyperparameter_transfer: muP tuned on a small proxy model and transferred to 7B

models.name: phi-3-medium
models.architecture: same tokenizer and architecture as phi-3-mini

other.tokens: 4.8T, same data for slightly more epochs

models.name: phi-3.5-MoE
models.architecture: MoE feed-forward layers, top-2 routing over 16 GLU experts

models.name: phi-3.5-mini
models.architecture: phi-3-mini with more multilingual and long-text mid-training data

models.name: phi-3.5-Vision
models.architecture: CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder plus phi-3.5-mini decoder; dynamic cropping; image and text tokens interleaved

other.phi3_5_vision_loss: next-token loss on text tokens only; image-token loss ignored

inference.prompting: few-shot prompts with k per benchmark (see table), from a Microsoft internal evaluation tool; no optimisation of the pipeline for phi-3; a 2-shot example is in Appendix A; vision evaluated 0-shot in Llava-1.5 setting

other.phone_test: 4-bit phi-3-mini on iPhone 14, A16 Bionic, native, offline, more than 12 tokens per second

metrics.name: accuracy on academic benchmarks
metrics.definition: k-shot accuracy per benchmark (MMLU 5-shot, HellaSwag 5-shot, GSM-8K 8-shot CoT, etc.)

metrics.name: RAI defect rates (DR-x)
metrics.definition: percentage of samples with harm severity (0 to 7) at least x; ungroundedness scored 0 to 4; GPT-4 simulates multi-turn conversations

eval.protocol: All numbers from the same internal pipeline; may differ from published numbers. Single run, no seeds or confidence intervals stated.

availability.data: not released (inferred: no data link or statement in the paper)

evidence.quote: we use few-shot prompts to evaluate the models, at temperature 0

results.claim: phi-3-mini scores 68.8% on MMLU 5-shot, close to Mixtral 8x7b (70.5) and GPT-3.5 (71.4).
results.setup: Internal few-shot pipeline, temperature 0, phi-3-mini 3.8B, 3.3T tokens
results.note: abstract rounds to 69%; Table 3 reports phi-3.5-mini 69

results.claim: phi-3-mini scores low on TriviaQA (5-shot) versus Mixtral 8x7b, showing limited stored factual knowledge.
phi-3-small (7B) and phi-3-medium (14B) reach 75.7 and 78.0 MMLU 5-shot.
results.table: Table (Section 3), row MMLU (5-Shot), columns Phi-3-small 7b 75.7 and Phi-3-medium 14b 78.0

results.claim: phi-3-mini on GSM-8K 8-shot CoT beats Mixtral 8x7b and GPT-3.5.
4-bit quantized phi-3-mini fits in about 1.8GB and runs over 12 tokens/s on an iPhone 14.
results.quote: achieving more than 12 tokens per second

results.claim: phi-3-medium gains less over phi-3-small than small over mini on some benchmarks, taken as a sign the mix is not yet data optimal at 14B.
results.setup: 3.8B to 7B to 14B on the same data recipe

results.claim: phi-3.5-MoE has 42B total parameters, 6.6B active, and scores 69.2 average vs GPT-4o-mini 74.9.
On RULER, phi-3.5 models drop sharply at 128K context.
Safety alignment reduces harmful response rates on the Microsoft red-team test.
results.setup: phi-3-mini before and after safety post-training, Figure 5

results.claim: phi-3-mini ungroundedness on internal RAI benchmark.

limits: Model is limited by size for factual knowledge, shown by low TriviaQA; authors suggest search-engine augmentation (Figure 6).
Language mostly restricted to English for phi-3-mini.
Benchmark numbers come from a Microsoft internal pipeline and may differ from published numbers; authors say they did no prompt optimisation for phi-3.
Training data, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, hardware and compute are not stated; data and recipe are not released.
Gains from 7B to 14B are smaller on some benchmarks, so the data mixture may not be data optimal at 14B.
Significant performance drop on RULER at 128K, attributed to missing high-quality long-context mid-training data.
Residual hallucination, bias, inappropriate content and safety issues remain; Phi-3.5-Vision sometimes answers harmful queries (captcha, scam images) and weak at high-level reasoning.
Contamination of benchmarks is not analysed in the paper (inferred: no such section).

terms.definition: calibrating training data, rather than compute or overtraining, to a given model scale; 'optimal' used in an aspirational sense
